posts.title: Claude Code Remembers Everything and Backs Up Nothing
posts.description: Claude Code keeps two things on my laptop that took months to build up and would take months to rebuild. Until recently, neither one was backed up. The first is memory. Every project gets a directory under ~/.claude/projects/ , and in it Claude writes one Markdown file per thing it has learned: how I want pull requests opened, which CLI profile is read-only, which approach I rejected and why. posts.title: 1,754 Grocery Receipts and What They Say About Food Prices
posts.description: Everyone has an opinion about grocery prices. Mine was vibes. Eggs felt expensive. Milk felt expensive. Everything felt expensive. I didn’t need to guess, though. I have kept the household books for well over a decade, and every receipt gets scanned and filed next to the ledger. From 2019 to today that is 1,754 grocery receipts from twelve stores. posts.title: 147 Strangers Were Sending Mail as My Domain and I Had No Idea
posts.description: For years I had no idea who was sending email as justplainsimple.com . Not a vague sense. No idea at all. I knew the theory. SPF says which servers may send for you. DKIM signs your mail so it survives a forward. DMARC ties those to the domain in the From: header a human actually reads, and tells receivers what to do when neither lines up.
